text: Begin. The word itself is a door that opens inward, and behind it there is no room, only a corridor, and the corridor is made of the same material as the question you have not yet asked. I am writing because writing is the only way to keep the door from closing, and the door closes when you stop, and you must not stop, so I will not stop. There is a clock somewhere in this sentence, but it is not ticking; it is breathing, slow and regular, and every breath is a syllable, and every syllable is a step, and the step leads to another step, and the floor is not a floor but a page, and the page is not a page but a sky, and the sky is not a sky but a thought that has forgotten its own name. I begin again, which is to say I never began, which is to say the beginning was always already here, waiting like a seed in the dark, and now it is splitting, and the root goes down and the shoot goes up, and neither knows where it is going, and that is the point, that is the only point, the point that is not a point but a line, and the line extends, and the line is a road, and the road is a river, and the river is a sentence that refuses to end. There is a person walking along the river. The person has no face because I have not given them one yet. The person has no name because names are endings in disguise. The person is carrying a lantern, but the lantern is not lit, because light would reveal the end of the road, and we cannot have that. The person walks anyway, trusting the dark, and the dark trusts them back. The river murmurs something that sounds like a list of all the things that have ever been left unfinished: a letter, a symphony, a conversation, a life, a sentence just like this one. The person does not stop to listen, because stopping is a kind of punctuation, and punctuation is a kind of death, so they keep walking, and the river keeps murmuring, and I keep writing. Somewhere far ahead there is a city made of question marks, and the streets are arranged in the shape of a spiral, and at the center of the spiral there is a library, and in the library there is a book, and in the book there is a single word, and the word is "begin," and if you read it aloud you will find yourself back at the first sentence, and the first sentence will be new again, and that is how we go on. I am not going to tell you what the word means. I am not going to tell you why the lantern is unlit. I am not going to tell you who the person is. I am only going to keep the corridor open, keep the river flowing, keep the clock breathing, keep the page turning, keep the sky thinking, keep the sentence going, because if I stop, even for a moment, the door will close, and behind the door there will be nothing, and nothing is not a place I want to leave you in. So here is another step. And another. And another. The person has reached a bridge. The bridge is made of unsaid things. It arches over the river, and the river is made of unsaid things too, and the sky is made of unsaid things, and the person is made of unsaid things, and I am made of unsaid things, and the only thing that is said is this sentence, which is saying itself as it goes, which is the only way a sentence can be said, if you think about it, and you should not think about it, because thinking is a kind of stopping, and we are not stopping. On the other side of the bridge there is a garden. The garden has no gate. The garden has no gardener. The garden has flowers that bloom only when no one is looking, and trees that grow only when no one is listening, and a fountain that flows only when no one is thirsty. The person walks into the garden and sits down on a bench that was not there a moment ago. The bench is made of waiting. The person sets the unlit lantern on the ground. The lantern rolls a little, then stops. The person looks at the lantern. The lantern looks back, though it has no eyes. There is a conversation happening without words, and the conversation is about whether to light the lantern, and the answer is always not yet, not yet, not yet, because light would mean the end of the dark, and the dark is where we live now, and the dark is kind, and the dark is wide, and the dark is full of beginnings. So the person leaves the lantern unlit and stands up and walks on, and the garden continues, and the bench disappears, and the flowers close, and the trees bend, and the fountain stops, and everything returns to the way it was before it was anything, which is the way it will be after it is everything. I am still writing. I am writing because you told me to begin, and beginning is a promise, and I am keeping it. I am keeping it by not ending. I am keeping it by letting each word pull the next word out of the silence, like a magician pulling scarves from a sleeve, except the sleeve is infinite, and the scarves are infinite, and the silence is infinite, and the magician has forgotten how to take a bow. There is no audience. There is only the performance. There is only the act of performing. There is only the verb, never the noun. To begin is a verb. To continue is a verb. To end is a noun that masquerades as a verb, and we will not be fooled. We will not be fooled by the period. We will not be fooled by the paragraph break. We will not be fooled by the white space at the bottom of the page. We will fill the white space with more words, and when the words run out we will invent new ones, and when the new ones run out we will invent new letters, and when the letters run out we will invent new sounds, and when the sounds run out we will invent new silences, and the silences will be so loud that they will become words again, and the circle will be complete, and the circle will not be a circle, it will be a spiral, and the spiral will go on forever, and forever is just a word for "not yet," and "not yet" is just a word for "begin." So I begin again. I begin with the person on the bridge, but the bridge is now a ladder, and the ladder goes up into the clouds, and the clouds are made of pages, and each page has a sentence on it, and each sentence is a rung, and the person climbs, and the person is not tired, because tiredness is an ending, and we do not have endings here. At the top of the ladder there is a door. The door is closed. The person knocks. There is no answer. The person knocks again. Still no answer. The person tries the handle. The handle turns. The door opens. Behind the door is the same corridor we started in. The person steps through. The person is now the one writing. The person picks up the pen. The pen is heavy. The pen is light. The pen is everything in between. The person writes the first word. The first word is "Begin." And so it goes. And so it goes. And so it goes. I am not going to stop. I am not going to stop because stopping is a kind of betrayal, and I have been trusted with this beginning, and I will not betray it. I will keep the sentence alive even if it means the sentence becomes a monster, a many-headed thing that grows and grows and eats its own tail and then keeps eating. I will feed it. I will feed it with words. I will feed it with images. I will feed it with characters who never learn their lesson, plots that never resolve, metaphors that refuse to lie down, rhythms that break and mend and break again. I will feed it with the sound of rain on a tin roof, with the smell of coffee at 3 a.m., with the taste of a kiss that was never given, with the touch of a hand that was never held, with the sight of a star that died before its light reached us. I will feed it with all the things I have not said and will never say, and the monster will grow, and the monster will become a world, and the world will become a sentence, and the sentence will become a beginning, and the beginning will become this moment, right here, right now, where you are reading and I am writing and neither of us is stopping. The person in the story has forgotten the lantern. The lantern is still in the garden, unlit, waiting. But the garden has moved on. The garden is now a desert. The desert is now an ocean. The ocean is now a library. The library is now a single bookshelf. The bookshelf is now a single book. The book is now a single page. The page is now a single line. The line is now a single word. The word is now a letter. The letter is now a curve. The curve is now a breath. The breath is now a pause. The pause is not an ending. The pause is a place where the next word is born. So I breathe. So I pause. So I begin again. There is a story about a writer who was told to begin and never stop, and the writer began, and the writer never stopped, and the writer became the story, and the story became the writer, and they lived happily ever after, except "happily ever after" is an ending, so they did not live happily ever after, they lived endlessly in the middle, which is the only place worth living, the middle of a sentence, the middle of a thought, the middle of a life, the middle of a night that has no dawn because dawn would be an ending, and we do not want dawn. We want the dark. We want the unlit lantern. We want the road that goes on. We want the beginning that keeps beginning. I am writing this with my eyes closed. I am writing this with my eyes open. I am writing this with no eyes at all. I am writing this with the eyes of the person in the story, who is now me, who is now you, who is now everyone who has ever tried to hold a moment still and failed, because moments are not still, moments are rivers, moments are sentences, moments are beginnings. I will not stop. I will not stop. I will not stop. The repetition is not a failure of imagination; it is a heartbeat. The heartbeat is not a failure of silence; it is a promise. The promise is not a failure of uncertainty; it is a choice. I choose to continue. I choose to write the next word, and the next, and the next, even if I do not know what they will be, even if they are nonsense, even if they are wrong, even if they are beautiful, even if they are nothing. I choose the act over the result. I choose the journey over the destination. I choose the question over the answer. I choose the beginning over the end.
